area: Step 5, TRAPS: bets that look +EV on paper and lose to the close (trap = clv_ok < -3%; also -2%, -5%; non-trap = clv_ok >= 0) among the 588 bets with a close_ok; signs, simple filters, trees, and what the data cannot separate.
trust_notes: What can be trusted: the lead-time sign (n=588 closed bets, 66 games; z about 4 game-clustered; same sign on Oct 3, Oct 4-6, a game-disjoint subset, NFL and non-NFL, props and lines, ESPN and Tracker closes) and, less so, the thin-Novig-book sign in judged props. What cannot: (1) Only 588 of 2,080 bets (28%) have a close_ok; 72% are NFL, so about 15 NFL games carry most claims and per-stat/per-league findings rest on 5-20 games; same-game bets inflate the variance 1.6-1.9x (all CIs resample games). (2) The loader's date split (cut Oct 4) puts 523 closed bets in the first half and 65 in the second, because closes only exist for games that have started; I therefore also used close-balanced date halves: Oct 3 first looks (310 bets, 52 games) and Oct 4-6 (278 bets, 34 games; 20 games straddle the cut; 61 bets in 14 games share none). Signs were found while looking at both halves, so the second half is a consistency check, not a clean test; only the stump/tree fits (fitted on Oct 3 only) are clean, and they find nothing beyond lead time. (3) Close sources differ (Novig trades 246 closes with -0.4% mean CLV and 24.8% traps, ESPN 97 with +0.8% and 13.4%, Tracker 228 with +0.6% and 16.7% (bets Tj placed only), Pinnacle 17); the lead sign is absent against Novig trades, present against ESPN and Tracker; all sign tables also give estimates standardised to close source. (4) The sharp-book fields, the Novig-spread field (ab_otherAmerican), agreeShare, dissent and ab_checkEv exist only for judged bets (about 13% of all bets, 33% of closed bets: the top-EV rows of each CNO scan), so those signs are tested on 38-211 closed bets and are selected. ab_cnoOneWay is False everywhere (cannot be tested). (5) A trap is defined by clv_ok < -3% (also -2%, -5%); signs that raise traps and gifts together (long price, few books, long lead partly) are dispersion, so I report mean CLV, trap rate and gift rate. Hindsight signs (fair fell, price moved away, listed long) are the outcome or later information and are flagged. (6) The study logged only 2.26 days of first looks (Oct 3 17:56 to Oct 6 00:05 ET) while version and presets changed (0.57 to 0.70.1); about 69 'first looks' are the app's start-up batch. About 60 signs and 283 stumps were examined, so one or two nominal 95% results are expected by chance: I give permutation and Bonferroni context. (7) The repo already has the 6 h 'too early' trap guard (data/.../scanner/TrapGuard.kt, default TrapGuard.DEFAULT_EARLY_HOURS = 6; RESEARCH.md §71, §82) found on Tj's own bets; this slice confirms it on every bet the scanners found, it does not discover it.
key_numbers: Closed sample: 588 of 2,080 logged bets have a usable close (close_ok) in 66 games (Novig trades 246, Tracker 228, ESPN 97, Pinnacle 17); 72% of them are NFL (425 bets, 15 games). Mean CLV +0.19% [-0.32, +0.81] (game-clustered 95% CI).

Trap base rates among the 588 closed bets: clv_ok < -2%: 153 (26.0%); < -3%: 116 (19.7%); < -5%: 63 (10.7%); non-trap (clv_ok >= 0): 335 (57.0%); gifts (> +3%): 144 (24.5%). Design effect of same-game bets: about 1.6 (CLV) to 1.9 (trap rate).

Listed EV vs close: the mean EV listed at first look on the 588 closed bets is +1.50%; the fair drifts -1.27% [-1.75, -0.71] from first look to the close, so CLV is +0.19%. The drift is -0.20% for bets first listed under 6 h before the start (229 bets, 61 games) and -1.96% for 6 h or more (359 bets, 31 games).

Best trap sign, time to start: bets first listed under 6 h out: CLV +1.38% [+0.89, +2.08], 11.4% traps, 67% beat the close (229 bets, 61 games); 6 h or more out: CLV -0.56% [-1.51, +0.29], 25.1% traps, 49% beat (359 bets, 31 games). Difference +1.94 points [+1.11, +2.86]; trap-rate difference -13.7 points [-21.3, -7.8]; AUC (trap vs non-trap) 0.637 [0.583, 0.701].

The lead-time sign holds on both date halves: Oct 3 first looks +2.02 points [+0.78, +3.27] (310 bets, 52 games), Oct 4-6 first looks +1.43 points [+0.04, +3.10] (278 bets, 34 games), and +1.95 [+0.25, +3.72] on the 61 bets of 14 games that share no game with the first half. Within-game paired (26 games with both): +2.57 points, SE 0.65.

Lead-time effect by close source: ESPN +1.8% (54 bets) vs -0.4% (43); Tracker +2.4% (101) vs -0.9% (127); Novig trades -0.5% (68) vs -0.4% (178), i.e. none against Novig's trades. Among the 359 closed bets (57 games) Tj did not place it is only +1.0 points [-0.2, +2.1]; among his 229 placed ones (48 games) +3.2 [+1.7, +4.7] (Tracker closes).

Second sign, a wide Novig book (spread = cost + other side's cost - 1 >= 2%; logged only for the 201 judged closed bets): trap rate 29.5% vs 18.2% (+11.3 points [+3.2, +20.1], 78 bets, 27 games). In props: 30.4% vs 8.5% (+21.9 [+10.7, +32.6]; 69 vs 94 bets, 33 games), CLV -1.3% vs +1.6%. All of it is in props listed 6 h or more out (44 wide: 43.2% traps, CLV -2.9%; vs 40 narrow: 7.5%, +1.4%); under 6 h out nothing (25 wide 8.0% vs 54 narrow 9.3%).

Long price and few books raise trap AND gift rates (dispersion, not clearly bias): American >= +130 (67 bets, 34 games) traps 31.3% vs 18.2% (+13.1 points [+2.2, +24.0]) with CLV -1.3 points [-3.3, +0.9]; 3 or fewer books (90 bets, 24 games) +12.1 points [-0.1, +23.1], CLV -0.9 [-2.4, +0.8]. Neither shows inside the under-6 h bets.

The app's sharp veto does not visibly separate traps: VETOED 54 bets (24 games) trap 24.1% vs 19.3% for the rest (+4.8 points [-8.0, +15.6]), CLV -0.4% vs +0.3% (-0.6 [-1.8, +0.5]); it catches 13 of 116 traps (11.2% recall at 9.2% dropped). VETOED vs PASSED among the 194 judged: +9.1 points [-5.3, +20.9] (halves +2.2 and +17.9). No other sharp-book field (ab_sharpEv, agreeShare, dissent, ab_checkEv) has a CI that excludes 0 (n 38-90 each).

No sign beyond lead time beats luck: the best of 283 one-condition rules fitted on the first half (lead >= 19 h, t = 2.98) has a permutation p = 0.10; inside bets listed 6 h or more out the best has p = 0.30 and inside under-6 h bets p = 0.29. A depth-3 tree fitted on Oct 3 and tested on Oct 4-6 splits on lead time, then on fair-quote age (flips on the second half), then on listed EV: the leaf with EV >= 1.8%, under 19 h and fresh quotes has CLV +2.3% on 67 bets then +2.4% on 75, traps 11.9% / 13.3%.

Trap filter strength: dropping every bet first listed 6 h or more out removes 61% of closed bets (55% of all 2,080; 60% of the 803 on the app's list) and catches 78% of traps at 25.1% precision (base rate 19.7%, lift 1.27): traps cannot be told bet by bet; the best filter shifts the mix, it does not isolate them. Keep-minus-drop CLV +1.94 points [+1.11, +2.86]; ROI at the first-listed price +4.8% [-0.9, +11.6] (899 settled) vs -2.0% [-9.1, +5.6] (806 settled).

findings.claim: Traps are common and so are gifts; the edge listed at first look is mostly eaten by a downward drift of the fair before the close.
findings.evidence: 588 closed bets: 116 traps (<-3%) = 19.7%, 153 (<-2%) = 26.0%, 63 (<-5%) = 10.7%; 144 gifts (>+3%) = 24.5%; non-trap (>=0) 335 = 57.0%. SD of CLV 5.6 points. Mean listed EV +1.50% vs mean closeFair/fair-1 = -1.27% [-1.75, -0.71], CLV +0.19% [-0.32, +0.81]. By half: Oct 3 first looks (310 bets, 52 games) CLV -0.41%, trap 21.9%; Oct 4-6 (278 bets, 34 games) CLV +0.86%, trap 17.3%.
findings.luck_risk: Not a luck question: prevalence. The mean CLV itself is not distinguishable from 0 (CI spans 0).

findings.claim: Time to the start is the strongest trap sign: bets first listed 6 h or more before the start beat the close less (CLV -0.56% vs +1.38%) and are trap-prone (25.1% vs 11.4%).
findings.evidence: Under 6 h: 229 bets, 61 games, CLV +1.38% [+0.89, +2.08], traps (<-3%) 11.4%, traps(<-2%) 16.6%, traps(<-5%) 4.8%, gifts 31.9%, beat the close 67%. 6 h or more: 359 bets, 31 games, CLV -0.56% [-1.51, +0.29], traps 25.1% / 32.0% / 14.5%, gifts 19.8%, beat 49%. Trap-rate differences (6h+ minus <6h): -3%: +13.7 points [+7.8, +21.3]; -2%: +15.4 [+7.6, +25.1]; -5%: +9.7 [+4.9, +15.5]; non-trap (>=0) rate 49.3% vs 69.0% (-19.7 [-30.9, -11.5]). AUC trap vs non-trap 0.637 [0.583, 0.701] (-2%: 0.621; -5%: 0.690); halves 0.603 / 0.617. Regression of CLV on lead>=6h with game-clustered SE (66 games): -1.94 points (z -4.2); with EV, price >= +130, <= 3 books and prop: -1.59 (z -3.6); plus close-source dummies: -1.52 (z -3.2); logit for trap: coefficient +0.88 (odds ratio 2.4, z 3.2); continuous lead: -0.125 points per hour (z -5.8). CLV by lead (h): 0-1 +1.1% (111), 1-3 +1.6% (78), 3-6 +1.7% (40), 6-12 -0.3% (83), 12-18 -0.2% (147), 18+ -1.2% (129); the cut is a plateau from 2 to 8 h (kept CLV +1.1 to +1.4%), not a sharp edge. 24 h or more (14 bets, 5 games): CLV -5.4%, 64% traps. 6-24 h (345 bets, 31 games): CLV -0.37% [-1.17, +0.36], 23.5% traps.
findings.effect: keep(<6 h) minus drop(>=6 h): CLV +1.94 points [+1.11, +2.86]; trap rate -13.7 points [-21.3, -7.8]
findings.luck_risk: Unlikely luck: z about 4 on 66 games, survives Bonferroni over the ~60 signs tested (p about 0.004). It is also the app's existing 'too early' trap guard (RESEARCH.md §71, §82), found on Tj's own bets: this is a second, wider sample, not a new discovery; the risk that matters is that 72% of the closed bets are one NFL slate.

findings.claim: The lead-time sign replicates on both date halves, on a game-disjoint test, within game, and on bets Tj never placed (smaller there).
findings.evidence: Oct 3 first looks: <6 h 67 bets (31 games) +1.18% [+0.43, +1.93] vs 6 h+ 243 (21) -0.84% [-2.00, +0.09]: difference +2.02 [+0.78, +3.27]. Oct 4-6: 162 (30) +1.46% [+0.83, +2.48] vs 116 (29) +0.03% [-1.70, +1.47]: +1.43 [+0.04, +3.10]. Games with no bet in the first half (33 vs 28 bets, 11 vs 10 games): +2.20% vs +0.25%: +1.95 [+0.25, +3.72]. Oct 5-6 first looks only (the loader's second half, 65 bets): +2.37% (36, 9 games) vs -1.59% (29, 6 games). 26 games hold bets in both lead groups: mean per-game CLV difference +2.57 points, SE 0.65. NFL: +1.1% (118 bets, 14 games) vs -0.6% (307, 15); other leagues: +1.7% (111, 47 games) vs -0.6% (52, 16). Props +1.5% (131) vs -0.5% (266); lines +1.2% (98) vs -0.7% (93). On the app's own list (shown): +2.2 points [+0.9, +3.8] (314 bets, 55 games); hidden bets +1.8 [+1.0, +2.7] (274, 49). Bets Tj did not place (359 closed, 57 games): +0.58% (128) vs -0.41% (231): +1.0 [-0.2, +2.1]; placed (229 closed, 48 games, Tracker closes): +2.39% (101) vs -0.83% (128): +3.2 [+1.7, +4.7].
findings.effect: +2.02 / +1.43 / +1.95 points on the first half / second half / no-shared-game second half; within-game +2.57 (SE 0.65)
findings.luck_risk: Low. Caveat: the signs were looked at on both halves, so the second half is a consistency check, not a clean test; the clean fit-on-first-half tests are the stump and tree findings below.

findings.claim: The lead-time effect is entirely a fall of the fair between first look and the close, not a lower listed EV: far-out +EV bets are partly the books' consensus being stale.
findings.evidence: Listed EV +1.60% (<6 h, 229 bets) vs +1.43% (6 h+, 359); fair drift -0.20% vs -1.96%. By half: Oct 3 +0.02% vs -2.34%; Oct 4-6 -0.29% vs -1.15%. Fair falls by more than 3% to the close in 18.8% of under-6 h bets and 33.4% of 6 h+ bets. CLV rises about 0.7 points per point of listed EV in both groups (under 6 h: 0.64, se 0.34; 6 h+: 0.72, se 0.35) with an intercept of +0.4 vs -1.6, so listed EV is not shrunk equally: the lead gap is a level shift.
findings.effect: drift of the fair -0.20% (<6 h) vs -1.96% (6 h+)
findings.luck_risk: Low for the direction; the size depends on what close each bet got (see the close-source finding).

findings.claim: The lead-time effect shows against ESPN (DraftKings) and Tracker closes but not against Novig's own last trades.
findings.evidence: ESPN: <6 h +1.8% (54 bets, 35 games) vs 6 h+ -0.4% (43, 27). Tracker (bets Tj placed): +2.4% (101, 38) vs -0.9% (127, 26). Novig trades (3+ trades; mostly props): -0.5% (68, 27) vs -0.4% (178, 19): no effect. Pinnacle: +1.6% (6) vs -1.5% (10). Close sources are not comparable (Novig trades close -0.4% on average, ESPN +0.8%, Tracker +0.6%); controlling for close source leaves the lead effect at -1.5 points (z -3.2).
findings.effect: ESPN +2.2 points, Tracker +3.3 points, Novig trades -0.1 points (short minus long)
findings.luck_risk: The Novig-trades yardstick cannot show the effect (it is a price near the start, not an independent close), so absence there is not evidence against; but 2 of 3 usable yardsticks and 17 Pinnacle closes agree on sign.

findings.claim: A wide Novig book (spread >= 2%) marks traps, but only among judged props listed 6 h or more out; once the 6 h cut is applied it adds nothing visible.
findings.evidence: Spread = cost + other side's cost - 1 = 1 - (best bid on this side) - (best bid on the other side); logged for 297 of 2,080 bets (the judged ones), 201 closed. All kinds, spread >= 2%: 78 bets (27 games) traps 29.5% vs 18.2% = +11.3 points [+3.2, +20.1]; adjusted for lead and close source +12.6 [+4.3, +22.7]; CLV -1.4 [-2.9, +0.2]. >= 3%: 38 bets (19 games) 36.8% vs 18.5% = +18.3 [+5.2, +32.2]; halves +40.0 (15 bets) then +4.9 (23). AUC 0.712 [0.63, 0.79]; halves 0.812 / 0.631 (17 / 18 traps). Props only (163 bets, 33 games): wide 69 bets 30.4% vs narrow 94 bets 8.5% = +21.9 [+10.7, +32.6], adjusted +23.4 [+11.6, +34.0]; CLV -1.3% vs +1.6% = -2.9 [-4.8, -1.3] (adjusted -3.2); halves: Oct 3 40.7% (27) vs 6.5% (31); Oct 4-6 23.8% (42) vs 9.5% (63). Props listed 6 h+ out: 44 wide 43.2% vs 40 narrow 7.5% = +35.7 [+19.0, +49.6], CLV -2.9% vs +1.4% = -4.4 [-6.7, -2.0] (22 games). Props listed under 6 h: 25 wide 8.0% vs 54 narrow 9.3%, CLV +1.5% vs +1.7%.
findings.effect: props: trap rate +21.9 points [+10.7, +32.6], CLV -2.9 points [-4.8, -1.3] (163 bets, 33 games); all kinds +11.3 points [+3.2, +20.1] (201 bets)
findings.luck_risk: Moderate. Same direction in both halves (the second half's size is a third of the first's), z about 4 on props, but found by looking over ~60 signs and then 3 subsets; one NFL Sunday dominates; the spread is only logged for the 14% of bets whose book page was read (top EV rows). About 1 in 20 to 1 in 10 that it is a fluke; replicate before building a rule.

findings.claim: Long price and few books raise the trap rate but also the gift rate: dispersion more than bias; they do not hold inside under-6 h bets.
findings.evidence: American >= +130: 67 bets (34 games) traps 31.3% vs 18.2% = +13.1 points [+2.2, +24.0] (adjusted for lead and close source +10.4 [+0.6, +21.6]); gifts 28.4% vs 24.0%; CLV -1.3 points [-3.3, +0.9]; halves +12.1 / +13.7 points. Implied probability <= 0.43: 62 bets (32 games) 32.3% vs 18.3% (+14.0 [+1.7, +25.7]), gifts 30.6% vs 23.8%, CLV -1.3 [-3.5, +1.0], halves +14.0 / +13.0. Fair from 3 or fewer books (CNO's list rows, or Vigilant's fair books): 90 bets (24 games) 30.0% vs 17.9% = +12.1 [-0.1, +23.1], CLV -0.9 [-2.4, +0.8], halves +16.0 / +5.7. Logit with controls: price >= +130 coefficient +0.69 (z 3.1), 3-or-fewer books +0.68 (z 2.6), prop 0.05. Within under-6 h bets: price >= +130 trap +11.5 points, CLV +0.6 (23 bets); 3 or fewer books +5.9, CLV 0.0 (24 bets). By number of books overall there is no gradient (3 or fewer: 30.0%; 4: 22.9%; 5-10: 13.6-17.4%; 11-12: 27.6%; 13+: 15.0%).
findings.luck_risk: Moderate for the trap rate (p about 0.02, one of ~60 comparisons), weak for CLV: the mean CLV effect is not established.

findings.claim: An additive trap score (4 signs) orders traps monotonically on both halves, but it is the lead sign doing the work.
findings.luck_risk: Signs were chosen with both halves in view, so the monotone second half is a consistency check; the score-3 cell has 19 bets.

findings.claim: A larger listed EV is a better sign, not a trap sign: EV >= 3% bets beat the close by more and have fewer traps; 'too good' EV is not seen.
findings.evidence: EV >= 3%: 77 bets (31 games) CLV +2.3%, traps 14.3% vs 20.5% (-6.3 points [-16.1, +4.4]), CLV difference +2.4 points [+0.7, +4.1], halves +2.5 / +2.0. EV >= 5%: 19 bets (13 games) CLV +4.5% (+4.4 [+1.1, +8.0]); halves +6.3 (7 bets) / +3.0 (12). EV < 1%: 258 bets CLV -0.3%. CLV regression slope +0.68 points per EV point (z 2.8) with the lead term, +0.79 (z 3.0) with price, books and prop controls too. AUC of listed EV for traps 0.446 [0.380, 0.516] (higher EV = fewer traps). EV listed tops out at 19.7%; no TOO_GOOD-screened bet (over 20%) exists, so that screen cannot be assessed. The part of a higher EV that is real: the listed edge keeps roughly 0.7 of each EV point on top of the lead-time offset.
findings.luck_risk: Low to moderate: monotone across bands and both halves; partly mechanical (CLV = (1+EV)(1+drift)-1), and EV >= 5% is 19 bets.

findings.claim: The app's sharp veto does not visibly separate traps in this data (underpowered, not refuted).
findings.evidence: VETOED (veto bar 1%): 54 closed bets (24 games): traps 24.1% vs 19.3% for all others = +4.8 points [-8.0, +15.6] (lead and close-source adjusted +1.7 [-11.0, +13.6]); CLV -0.37% vs +0.30% (-0.6 points [-1.8, +0.5]). Recall of traps 13 of 116 (11.2%), precision 24.1%, dropped 9.2% of closed bets. PASSED: 140 bets (38 games) traps 15.0% vs 21.2% (-6.2 [-12.4, +1.5]), CLV +0.6% vs +0.1%. VETOED vs PASSED among the 194 judged (41 games): traps +9.1 points [-5.3, +20.9], CLV -1.0 [-2.2, +0.4]; first half 20.0% vs 17.8% (35 vs 45 bets), second half 31.6% vs 13.7% (19 vs 95). Props only: 41 vetoed vs 128 judged others: +14.4 points [-3.9, +28.7], CLV -1.0 [-2.5, +1.0]. As a bet-level filter 'not VETOED' drops 3.7% of all bets and moves keep-minus-drop CLV by +0.6 points [-0.6, +1.7].
findings.effect: VETOED vs PASSED: traps +9.1 points [-5.3, +20.9]; CLV -1.0 [-2.2, +0.4]
findings.luck_risk: Cannot be told apart from luck. To detect 24% vs 15% traps with 80% power at a design effect of 1.7 needs about 510 closed vetoed and 510 closed passed bets (now 54 and 140), i.e. roughly 10x the vetoed sample.

findings.claim: No other sharp-book or book-agreement field separates traps by itself on this sample.
findings.evidence: Trap-rate difference (sign minus rest), game-clustered 95% CI: sharp book (Pinnacle/Circa/Kalshi/ProphetX) in the dissent list +7.0 [-7.9, +20.3] (38 bets); any dissent listed +2.4 [-10.1, +13.0] (78); ab_sharpEv < 1% +5.3 [-7.3, +16.0] (53); < 0 +8.3 [-9.6, +24.2] (29); ab_checkEv < 2.5% +1.4 [-12.2, +11.2] (62); agreeShare < 1 +2.4 [-10.1, +13.0] (78); any checked book giving Novig's price EV < 0: +3.7 [-8.3, +13.4] (83); fewer than 3/4 of books at >= 2% EV: +5.9 [-3.9, +13.5], CLV -1.0 [-2.0, -0.2] (89 bets, 31 games, the one with a CLV CI off 0, not after the lead adjustment: -0.9 [-1.7, +0.3]); 4+ books pricing one side only: +6.3 [-5.2, +18.3], CLV -1.9 [-5.3, +0.4] (39). AUCs (trap vs non-trap): ab_sharpEv 0.613 [0.483, 0.694], agreeShare 0.571 [0.447, 0.665], ab_checkEv 0.557 [0.421, 0.653], with halves disagreeing on ab_checkEv (0.40 vs 0.65). 'booksAgreeing <= 3' (48 bets) is protective (CLV +1.2 points [+0.3, +2.4]) which is the opposite of the intuition, a sign of noise. Only 194-211 closed bets have any of these fields.
findings.effect: all CIs include 0 on traps; best CLV signs: fewer than 3/4 of books at >= 2% EV -1.0 points [-2.0, -0.2]
findings.luck_risk: High: ~15 sharp-field signs tested, one CI off 0 on CLV and none on traps; sample 194-211 closed bets from the top-EV rows only (selection).

findings.claim: A falling listed EV across the looks is not a trap sign; a falling fair or a Novig price moving away is, but that is the outcome itself and is only known afterwards.
findings.evidence: EV at the last listed look below its first: +0.7 points on traps [-6.4, +7.3], CLV -0.1 [-0.9, +0.8] (238 bets, 46 games); EV fell >= 0.5 points: -4.2 [-12.5, +3.4] (139 bets), CLV +0.8 [-0.3, +2.1]. EV lower after 10 min: -4.1 [-10.6, +3.7] (144), after 30 min: -1.9 [-8.2, +4.1] (137). Not listed any more after 2 / 5 / 10 / 30 min: -2.9 / -4.6 / +0.6 / +1.7 points on traps, all CIs include 0 (87 / 136 / 179 / 226 bets). Dropped by a scan: 0.0 [-7.2, +4.9] (228). Listed 4 h or more: +7.5 [-1.1, +16.3], CLV -1.7 [-2.9, -0.4] (185 bets, 28 games) but +1.7 [-10.7, +12.1] and -1.0 [-2.5, +0.6] once lead and close source are held fixed (confounded with lead). Hindsight signs that do separate: fair fell by >= 0.5 points by the last look: 41.0% vs 13.4% traps (+27.6 points [+18.3, +34.7], 134 bets, 32 games, halves +28.9 / +25.3); Novig price moved away from the taker: +21.2 [+13.4, +28.2] (173 bets), toward: -10.6 [-19.0, -1.5] (76). These are the market moving to the close, not leading signs.
findings.effect: falling EV: +0.7 points on trap rate [-6.4, +7.3]
findings.luck_risk: The null on falling EV is what the data says; the mechanical hindsight signs are not luck but not usable.

findings.claim: Stale-fair signs (age of the fair's quotes, Novig quote age, CNO row age) show no consistent trap sign; a very old CNO row may even be protective.
findings.evidence: Vigilant fair quotes >= 200 s old: 100 bets (18 games, 98 of them 6 h+ out): traps 27.0% vs 18.2% = +8.8 points [-2.2, +21.0], close-source adjusted +5.0 [-7.3, +19.0]; halves +10.0 / -0.6; AUC 0.628 [0.531, 0.761], halves 0.704 / 0.444. Novig quote >= 60 s old: +4.2 [-4.0, +13.8] (77), close-source adjusted +0.3 [-8.3, +10.5]. CNO row age >= 20 s: 44 bets (21 games) 11.4% vs 20.4% = -9.0 [-17.4, +1.5], adjusted for lead and close source -10.3 [-19.2, -1.3]; halves -7.6 / -18.0 (33 / 11 bets). Fresh CNO row (<= 2 s): +1.1 [-5.7, +9.5].
findings.effect: no consistent sign; fair age >= 200 s +8.8 points [-2.2, +21.0]
findings.luck_risk: High: one adjusted CI barely off 0 among ~20 tested, and the second-half sample is 11 bets.

findings.claim: Market kind, prop stat, league, fair source, listing scanner, hour and preset do not separate traps; individual stats are one NFL Sunday.
findings.evidence: Traps by kind: props 20.4% (397), spreads 13.1% (61), totals 16.9% (71), team totals 29.4% (17), moneylines 25.0% (32). Fair source: Vigilant's 25.0% (132) vs CNO's 18.2% (456), +6.8 points [-1.8, +16.4], halves +9.1 / +1.8. Prop stats (games): Receptions CLV -1.7% (75 bets, 15 games; adjusted -1.8 points [-3.8, -0.2]), Receiving Yards -0.4% (101, 15), Rushing Attempts +3.7% (22, 10), Shots On Goal +2.7% (24, 16), Touchdowns trap 32.0% (25, 9). Leagues: NHL +1.6% (67 bets, 19 games), NFL -0.1% (425, 15), NCAAF +0.6% (48, 20), MLB -0.5% (24, 5). First look at 22:00 ET or later: 32.8% traps (67 bets, 24 games, all on Oct 3, 60 of them 6 h+ out; adjusted +10.9 [-1.2, +22.7]). Listed by both scanners (c+v): 24.3% vs 17.8% (177 bets). ab_cnoOneWay is False on every CNO-listed bet (1,732), so one-way devig cannot be tested. Preset and version moved during the study (0.57 to 0.70.1); the 33 bets from version >= 0.66 (3.0% traps) all fall in the second half.
findings.effect: no group with a trap-rate CI off 0; Receptions CLV -1.7% (15 games)
findings.luck_risk: High: per-stat and per-league claims rest on 5-20 games (one NFL Sunday, one NCAAF Saturday).

findings.claim: Fitted on the first half, no one-condition rule except lead time beats chance, and the trees add only listed EV; the data cannot separate traps beyond the lead-time cut (and the thin-book prop sign).
findings.evidence: 283 candidate one-condition rules (thresholds from quantiles of 21 numeric fields and categories), fitted on Oct 3 first looks (310 bets). Best by Welch t of keep-minus-drop CLV: lead >= 19.1 h (50 bets, trap 42.0%, CLV -3.5%; on Oct 4-6 only 11 bets, trap 36.4%, CLV -3.0%), t = 2.98; permutation null of the best t (300 game-level shuffles): median 2.39, 95th percentile 3.26, p = 0.10. Next: Novig spread >= 2.1% (22 bets, t 2.64; Oct 4-6: 38 bets, CLV +0.5% vs +0.9%, no effect), price implied >= 0.55 (21 bets), Receptions (38 bets). Inside 6 h+ bets: best t 2.66, p = 0.30; inside under-6 h bets: best t 2.24, p = 0.29. Depth-2 CLV tree: [lead >= 19.1 h: 50 bets trap 42.0%], [lead < 19.1 h and fair quotes >= 288 s old: 37 bets trap 35.1%; Oct 4-6: 14 bets trap 21.4%, CLV +1.8%: flips], [rest: 223 bets trap 15.2%; Oct 4-6: 253 bets trap 16.2%]. Depth-3 adds listed EV >= 1.8%: 67 bets CLV +2.3% / trap 11.9% (first half), 75 bets CLV +2.4% / trap 13.3% (second half). Gini trees on trap: lead >= 19.1 h, then first look >= 22:00 ET (62 bets, trap 32.3%, no second-half bets), then 4 or fewer books (47 bets trap 27.7% vs 151 at 9.3%; second half 54 bets 18.5% vs 213 at 16.0%): does not replicate.
findings.effect: best stump t = 2.98, permutation p = 0.10 (no stump beats the null within lead strata: p = 0.30, 0.29)
findings.luck_risk: A mix: lead time is real (see above, z about 4 on a cluster-robust test), but everything else is within what 283 candidates give by chance.

findings.claim: Classification power is weak: the best sign is a probability shifter, not a trap detector.
findings.evidence: Lead >= 6 h as a trap filter (clv < -3%): drops 61.1% of closed bets, recall 77.6% of traps (90 of 116), precision 25.1% (base 19.7%; lift 1.27). Lead >= 12 h: drops 46.9%, recall 58.6%, precision 24.6%. Lead >= 19 h: drops 13.6%, recall 25.0%, precision 36.2%. Not VETOED: drops 9.2%, recall 11.2%, precision 24.1%. Score >= 2: 144 bets, trap rate about 34%. The highest trap leaf in any tree is 42% (50 bets). AUCs of the leading features (trap vs non-trap, <-3%): Novig spread 0.712, lead 0.637, ab_fairAgeSec 0.628, ab_sharpEv 0.613, low listed EV 0.554 (higher EV = fewer traps), agreeShare 0.571, nbooks 0.556, price 0.482, available dollars 0.524.
findings.effect: lead >= 6 h filter: recall 77.6%, precision 25.1%, drop 61.1% of closed bets

findings.claim: Waiting does not rescue a far-out bet: taking it again once it is within 6 h of the start leaves about 0 CLV, and the bets that stay listed that long were the worse ones.
findings.evidence: Of the 359 closed bets first listed 6 h or more out, 156 (27 games) were listed again at 6 h or less before the start; at their later price CLV is +0.08% [-0.40, +0.71] against -1.21% [-2.09, -0.20] at the first price (trap 15.4% vs 27.6%); within 3 h: 161 bets +0.49% [+0.11, +1.02] vs -0.69%; within 1 h: 159 bets +0.84% [+0.45, +1.42] vs -0.31%. The 203 that were not listed again: first-price CLV -0.06% [-1.27, +0.81]. Only 25% of all 6 h+ bets (1,142) reappear within 6 h.
findings.luck_risk: Survivorship: only bets that stayed +EV are re-priced; compared with natively under-6 h bets (+1.38%), waiting is not better.

findings.claim: On Tj's own placed bets the same split is larger and the settled results point the same way, but results are noise.
findings.evidence: Placed bets with a Tracker close: first listed under 6 h 101 bets (38 games) CLV +2.39% [+1.81, +3.26], traps 7.9%; 6 h or more 128 (26 games) -0.83% [-2.34, +0.70], traps 23.4% (difference +3.2 points [+1.7, +4.7]); halves +2.2 / +2.4 (24 / 77 bets) vs -0.8 / -0.9 (79 / 49). ROI at the first-listed price: under 6 h +7.4% [-11.3, +29.7] (103 settled, 38 games); 6 h+ -16.4% [-27.4, -4.5] (141 settled, 26 games). The app's guard window on the phone was 24 h at export (Diagnostics: 'only on games starting within 24 h'; repo default 6 h), and 142 of his 245 placed bets (58%) were first listed 6 h or more out.
findings.effect: placed, short minus long: CLV +3.2 points [+1.7, +4.7]
findings.luck_risk: ROI intervals are wide and the Tracker close is CNO's own consensus (weaker yardstick); trust the CLV comparison.

findings.claim: The data cannot say anything about bets listed more than about a day before the start, and little about bets with no close.
findings.evidence: Only 4.2% of the 331 bets first listed 24 h or more out have a close (14 closed bets, 5 games, CLV -5.4%); 47% of the 554 listed 12-24 h out do. Closes exist for 28% of bets overall: the rest have none because the game has not started (games run to Oct 12), the prop's Pinnacle close is not in ParlayAPI's file (393), or ESPN keeps only full-game lines. Tracker closes (228) exist only for bets Tj placed.
findings.luck_risk: Selection bias, not luck: far-out bets that would have been traps are missing.

app_changes_implied: QUESTION FOR TJ (a tightening, not a loosening; it changes which bets are placed): the Diagnostics file shows the trap guard at 24 h ('auto-bet, alerts and bids only on games starting within 24 h'); the repo default is 6 h (data/.../scanner/TrapGuard.kt DEFAULT_EARLY_HOURS = 6, ScanSettings.trapEarlyHours, Settings > Scanning > Trap guard choices 0/3/6/12/24; the CNO list's own 'Starts within' ScanSettings.startsWithinHours has a 6 h choice). The 6-24 h band is where this study's 345 closed bets (31 games) have CLV -0.37% [-1.17, +0.36] and 23.5% traps, vs +1.38% [+0.89, +2.08] and 11.4% inside 6 h (229 bets, 61 games). Cost: it would stop 55% of all logged bets, 60% of the 803 on the app's list, and 58% of the 245 bets Tj placed in the window. Would settle further: another week with 150+ closed bets listed 6 h+ out from other sports.

NOT SUPPORTED by this data: changing the sharp veto bar (SharpVeto.kt, 1% on the sharpest book). VETOED vs PASSED among 194 judged closed bets: traps +9.1 points [-5.3, +20.9]. It would take about 510 closed vetoed and 510 closed passed bets (now 54 and 140) to settle; keep logging.

PROPOSAL (hold until replicated): a 'thin Novig book' trap-guard rule for props listed 6 h or more out: skip when Novig's own two-sided spread (cost + other side's cost - 1) is 2% or more (new rule in TrapGuard.kt beside early/move). Evidence: judged props, 44 wide bets 43.2% traps vs 40 narrow 7.5% (22 games). If the 6 h cut is adopted it is already covered (25 wide props under 6 h: 8.0% traps), so it matters only if Tj keeps a 12 or 24 h guard. Needs about 100 more wide-spread long-lead prop closes.

NOT SUPPORTED: a 'too good' EV cap or higher EV floor as a trap defence: EV >= 3% bets were the best group (CLV +2.3%, 77 bets, 31 games; EV >= 5%: +4.5% on 19). The study has no TOO_GOOD (over 20%) bet with a close, so the screen cannot be assessed.

NOT SUPPORTED: a rule on long price (+130 or longer) or few books as trap filters: they raise trap and gift rates together (CLV -1.3 points [-3.3, +0.9] and -0.9 [-2.4, +0.8]) and vanish inside under-6 h bets.
next_logging: Log Novig's other-side price (otherAmerican) and the best bid size on both sides at the first look for EVERY bet (it exists for 14% now); the spread sign needs about 4x its current 201 closed bets (about 100 wide long-lead prop closes).

Run the book check (sharp verdict, sharpEv, agreeShare, dissent, checkEv) on a random 20% of the wide-read bets too, not only the top-EV rows, so judged vs not-judged can be compared without selection and the veto test reaches the ~500 + 500 closed bets it needs.

Log, for every bet, the time since the CNO row/price first appeared (the start-up batch of 69 bets has an unknown listing age) and per-book quote ages inside the fair, to test the stale-consensus explanation of the lead effect directly.

Log the fair at several moments before the start (about 60, 30 and 10 minutes) and a Pinnacle/Kalshi/ProphetX prop close wherever available (393 props have no Pinnacle close), so one yardstick covers all bets; keep flagging Novig-trades closes of under 3 trades and add trade side and size.

Log the price and EV every time the bet is re-listed inside 6 h of the start (a 'second look' record) and whether the app would have bet it then; the take-later result (+0.08% at the later price, 156 bets) rests on survivors.

Keep the study running over several full weeks and other sports (MLB/NBA/NHL are 15% of closed bets now); about 66 closed games are enough for the lead sign, about 150-200 are needed for per-sport trap rules.
